A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. The covering follows the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration. Material reference: use @Image1 only for the material of the chitin plates: their color, surface texture and seams. Do not copy its body, head, legs or shape; the creature is the brown bear described above.

spark_open.description: The creature is a quadrupedal hybrid shown in right-facing profile walking forward. It has the dense, shaggy brown fur, head, legs, paws and short tail of a bear, but its entire back from the shoulders to the rump is covered by a large, glossy, dark reddish-brown beetle exoskeleton, and a single long, curved, glossy beetle horn projects upward and forward from the center of its forehead. The fur is light tan on the muzzle and darker brown on the limbs and body, with a thick ruff around the neck. The beetle shell is highly reflective with longitudinal striations and consists of a smooth domed section over the shoulders and a larger oval section over the back, with a serrated lower margin where it meets the fur.
